landing.schemaDescription: An unofficial, source-led guide to The Freak Circus, an 18+ psychological horror visual novel by Neko Bueno.
landing.heroSubtitle: The Circus Is Open. Choose Who You Trust.
landing.heroLead: The Freak Circus is a world where romance and horror collapse into one. {pierrot}'s silent devotion curdles into obsession, {harlequin}'s charm hides danger — and as the {jester}, {doctor}, and {ticketTaker} enter the ring, the café-worker protagonist is pulled deeper into a spell where love may be as dangerous as it is real.
landing.whatP1: The Freak Circus is an 18+ psychological horror visual novel set around a circus that turns affection into danger. A café worker crosses paths with Pierrot, a silent yandere clown, and is pulled into his escalating rivalry with the seductive Harlequin.
landing.whatP2: The current prototype introduces five distinct performers, blends character-driven choices with unsettling imagery, and leaves its larger routes and endings in development. It is a story about obsession, masks, secrets, and deciding which smile is safe to trust.

whatFeatures.title: Psychological Horror
whatFeatures.text: Romance and dread share the same stage as affection slips into control, manipulation, and fear.

whatFeatures.title: Character-Driven Story
whatFeatures.text: Pierrot and Harlequin anchor the rivalry while Jester, Doctor, and Ticket Taker deepen the circus mystery.

whatFeatures.title: Meaningful Choices
whatFeatures.text: Dialogue and route decisions change encounters, reveal scenes, and shape the outcomes available in the current build.

whatFeatures.title: Dark Circus Atmosphere
whatFeatures.text: Original character art, theatrical tents, animated scenes, and a sinister fairground mood define the experience.

faq.a: The Freak Circus is an 18+ psychological horror visual novel created by Neko Bueno and published by Garula. Its current story centers on a café worker, Pierrot, and Harlequin.
No. The official itch.io listing labels it a prototype and says the remaining script and endings are still in development.

faq.q: Where should I play or download it?
faq.a: Use Garula’s official itch.io page. This guide does not host or redistribute game files.
The developer is working on the next chapter, but no release date is published on the official sources tracked here.

faq.q: Which characters appear in the current build?
faq.a: The current prototype introduces Pierrot, Harlequin, Jester, Doctor, and Ticket Taker. Columbina is also referenced in official maintenance notes.

faq.q: Does every character have a completed route?
faq.a: No. The official listing names planned Pierrot, Harlequin, and protagonist endings, while confirming that the remaining script and endings are still in development.
The current official listing names English, Brazilian Portuguese, and Chinese.
The official listing currently includes HTML5 browser play, Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.

faq.q: Is The Freak Circus suitable for younger players?
faq.a: No. The developer rates the game 18+ and lists dark themes including blood, death, kidnapping, cannibalism, non-consensual use of drugs, physical domination, and mild physical harassment / non-consensual physical contact.

faq.q: Where can I follow verified game updates?
faq.a: Use the developer’s itch.io devlog and official Tumblr. This site’s Updates section links its summaries back to those original posts.

faq.q: What can I find on this website?
faq.a: The site provides an in-page player, character profiles, a source-led Wiki, Day 3 status, an official download guide, update summaries, and community fan art.
No. This is an independent fan guide that links back to the developer’s official sources.

characters.pierrot: A sorrowful clown concealing profound emotions beneath a painted grin. His tale unfolds through love, loss, and the burden of secrets long kept.
characters.harlequin: A playful trickster whose lighthearted exterior conceals a far more intricate soul. Her bond with Pierrot lies at the very center of the story.
characters.jester: The circus's storyteller and silent witness, unraveling Columbina's tragic legend through puppet shows that expose the show's darkest truths.
characters.the-doctor: A plague doctor performing sinister experiments within the Cyan Tent, studying fear itself and probing the darker edges of medical ethics.
characters.ticket-taker: A manipulator of reality who presides over the Tent of Mirrors, using warped reflections to unmask the true face of every monster.

wiki.lead: A living reference for the current public build—written around primary sources and explicit content boundaries, not invented lore.
wiki.overview1: The protagonist works at a café. On the way to work, they meet Pierrot, a silent yandere whose fixation starts the central conflict. Harlequin, Pierrot’s seductive stage rival, enters the competition around the protagonist.
wiki.overview2: The official listing currently says all five character introductions are complete, one bad ending is available, and the rest of the script and endings are still being developed. The planned endings named there are Pierrot, Harlequin, and protagonist endings.
wiki.castText: These five characters have introductions in the current prototype. “Introduced” does not automatically mean a completed route or ending.
wiki.columbina: Columbina appears in official maintenance notes: the February 2026 Chinese-language update mentions a previously incomplete line when her name was entered. This confirms dialogue context, but it does not support the extensive backstory previously published on this site.
wiki.warning: The developer labels the game 18+. The official page warns about themes and scenes that may not be suitable for every player.
warnings: Non-consensual use of drugs, physical domination, and mild physical harassment / non-consensual physical contact

about.s0: About The Freak Circus: Story, Characters & Game
about.s1: Learn about The Freak Circus, its psychological horror story, the rivalry between Pierrot and Harlequin, its circus cast, and current game content.

about.s23: The short version of the site
about.x0: An independent, fan-maintained guide to The Freak Circus with a focus on useful context, clear sourcing, and honest limits.
about.x1: Information about The Freak Circus is spread across playable builds, development notes, and community conversation. This site brings the questions players actually ask into one readable place: who the characters are, what the current build contains, where Day 3 stands, and how to play on a suitable platform.
about.x2: Organising that information is not the hard part. The hard part is staying restrained while the information is still incomplete. The game is mid-development: of five introduced characters, only two have planned routes; of four announced endings, one is implemented; Day 3 is still being made and has no date. Under those conditions it is easy to find guides that look complete while being substantially guesswork.
about.x3: That is why this site treats "how far can we confirm" as the more important question than "how much can we write". An honest answer and a confident-sounding guess are worth very different amounts to a reader, and only one of them can be acted on.
about.x4: Material reproducible in a public build is described as current content. Developer intentions that have not shipped are labelled as planned or in development. Community theories, unsupported route names, and claims that cannot be reproduced in play are not rewritten as facts.
about.x5: In practice that shows up as follows. Character pages state the official height and age order, and separately flag which appearance and relationship details come from the fandom wiki rather than from the developer. The endings page states that exactly one ending is playable and lists the four planned ones separately, rather than implying that multiple endings can be reached today.
about.x6: What we decline to repeat matters just as much. The following circulate across fan sites as settled fact, but none of them have a first-party source, so this site does not present them as conclusions:
about.x7: This is the point most often misread about this site, so it is worth stating plainly. Right now the game has one implemented ending, and the scripts for both romance routes are still being written. Where there is no trigger, there is no honest trigger chart.
about.x8: Guides that specify picking a red balloon or avoiding defiance on Day 2 are describing a public build that does not exist. A reader who follows them finds no route at all, which is more confusing than having no guide in the first place. This site will add the real choices, scenes, and save points once the routes actually ship.
about.x9: Primary sources are the developer\'s itch.io page and devlog, and the official Tumblr FAQ and AMA posts. The height chart and age order quoted on the character pages come from images and answers published by the developer directly, not from sprite estimates or fan compilations.
about.x10: Every page that cites a specific fact links the source it came from, so you can check it independently rather than taking our word for it.
about.x11: This is not the developer, publisher, or an official support channel, and it does not present itself as one. Explanations and organization are independent editorial work; the game, characters, artwork, and related marks remain the property of their respective rights holders.
about.x12: The developer has stated that the itch.io page is the only official page for the game and has asked that it not be re-uploaded or reposted, and has confirmed that no official Discord server exists — so any server or account not linked from the official pages should be treated as fan-run or unauthorized.
about.x13: This site does not host game files and does not mirror the download packages. The optional player on the site is served by a third-party host, which the privacy policy covers.
about.x14: The site does not repackage or host game files, and it does not turn fan work found online into an unlicensed house gallery. Community selections are curated by hand, remain the work of their creators, and are withheld when source, permission, or attribution is unclear.
about.x15: Some appearance and relationship detail on the character profiles comes from the fandom wiki. That material is labelled as fan-derived on the page and kept visually separate from developer-confirmed facts, so a reader can decide how much weight to give it.
about.x16: Version-sensitive information is maintained through the on-site Updates and Day 3 pages. Character profiles state where the evidence ends instead of inventing endings simply to make a page look complete.
about.x17: The game is still a prototype, and its script, labels, and save behaviour can change between builds. If a page here conflicts with the current build, please say so.
about.x18: If a page conflicts with the current build, lacks important context, or needs an attribution correction, use the Contact page and identify the affected page and specific issue. Reproducible, well-located reports are reviewed first.
about.x19: Additions are welcome too. If there is a question you want answered here and no page covers it yet, tell us.
